To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presence or absence itself of laboratory measurements in an ICU patient profile is informative, (2) this information can be considered a predictor of in hospital mortality and 30 day post ICU discharge mortality, (3) the predictive power of this information is comparable to the measured laboratory data itself, and (4) this information is additive to the predictive power of measured laboratory data.
the presence or lack of laboratory test measurements can be informative and can be used as a potential predictor of patient mortality.
missing data in ICU patient profiles is informative and can convey information about a patient's health status and mortality risk, and can be used as a predictor in mortality risk prediction models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
missing data and its potential information.
the problem of missing data in ICU EHRs and the potential of using the information in missingness to improve the prediction performance of ICU mortality.
the problem of missing data in ICU data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence or the absence of a laboratory test can be a potential predictor of mortality and the inclusion of the indicator in a prediction model improves its performance.
the missingness of data is informative and can convey additional information to the observed data.
the presence of missingness indicators can be informative and can be a potential predictor of ICU mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absence of a laboratory test measurement can be informative and can be used as a predictor of mortality in the ICU.
the missing data in ICU patient profiles can be a potential source of hidden information and should be investigated further.
the absence of a variable recording itself can convey important information and can be a predictor in the context of intensive care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the presence or absence information of a predictor in a patient profile as a feature in itself to improve predictive models.
missingness itself can be a predictor and can be informative.
the presence or the absence of a variable itself might convey useful information about a patient health status.
